SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: He reports that his low back pain began on 05/04/2026. He describes moderate lumbar discomfort radiating slightly to the buttocks, worsened by prolonged sitting. He started NSAIDs today for pain relief.
Exam: Lower extremity strength 5/5, reflexes 2+, sensation intact. No spinal tenderness or muscle spasm noted.
Assessment: Acute low back pain, likely muscular/lumbar strain.
Plan: Continue NSAIDs as needed. Initiate physical therapy twice weekly. Return in two weeks for follow‑up.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: The patient returns after two weeks of NSAIDs and physical therapy. He notes mild improvement with NSAIDs but persistent discomfort.
Exam: Strength remains 5/5, reflexes normal, no neurologic deficits.
Assessment: Subacute low back pain with partial response to NSAIDs and no improvement after physical therapy.
Plan: NSAIDs were started on 05/05/2026 and continued through 06/15/2026 with partial relief. He completed a course of physical therapy consisting of 10 sessions that started on 05/11/2026 and ended on 06/15/2026, with no improvement in symptoms. Consider obtaining lumbar MRI to further evaluate.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient reports ongoing low back pain despite completed treatments. Denies any new symptoms.
Exam: Neuro exam normal lower-extremity strength, reflexes and sensation.
Assessment: Persistent low back pain without red flags.
Plan: He denies any red flag symptoms including trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit. Continue activity modification and consider MRI if symptoms persist.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient continues to experience lumbar pain; prior conservative measures have failed.
Exam: Unchanged neurologic exam.
Assessment: Low back pain refractory to NSAIDs and physical therapy, needing further anatomic localization.
Plan: The MRI will be used to localize the level prior to a planned L4-L5 epidural steroid injection. Schedule lumbar MRI today.
